title: IP update from Alphacore at DAC 2026
gist: Daniel Payne relays an interview from DAC 2026 with Alphacore's technical marketing director on its AMS, RF, imaging and rad-hard IP, foundry coverage, AI's role in EDA and IP, and a roadmap toward reconfigurable data-converter IP at 64 GS/s. The piece is largely a company update.

insights.claim: Alphacore supplies IP for AMS, RF, imaging and rad-hard designs to both commercial and military markets.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Niche rad-hard and mixed-signal IP serves defense/space demand that general IP vendors under-serve.

insights.claim: Alphacore's founders have a rad-hard background, its early work was on DOD contracts, and the company has grown organically without venture capital.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A bootstrapped, defense-rooted IP vendor has a different risk and funding profile than VC-backed peers.

insights.claim: Alphacore's IP is supported on GF 22FDX and 12nm, TSMC 28nm and 12/6FFC for automotive, STMicroelectronics FD-SOI, X-Fab and Tower Semi.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Shows multi-foundry reach, including specialty and FD-SOI nodes.

insights.claim: Alphacore also offers custom ASIC services and IP block customization alongside its catalog IP.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne

insights.claim: For radar designs needing high spurious-free dynamic range, Alphacore plans an on-chip demonstration where its IP takes SFDR from 45 dB to 75 dB.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: A 30 dB SFDR gain, if demonstrated, would be a notable radar and RF differentiator.

insights.claim: Alphacore expects reconfigurable data-converter IP for communication and sensing beyond 5G and 6G, with one chip providing multiple functions and a goal of 64 Giga-Samples per second.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Reconfigurable high-rate converters point to where RF/AMS IP demand is heading.

themes.theme: AI in EDA and IP at DAC 2026

insights.claim: Alphacore saw AI as a big theme at DAC 2026, whereas DAC 2025 emphasized chiplets and had little agentic AI.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Conference focus shifted from chiplets to AI within a year, a sentiment indicator for EDA.

insights.claim: On a DAC panel titled 'Build vs Buy: Who Owns the Intelligence Behind Tomorrow's Chips?', Alphacore's representative argued AI must be adopted for EDA and IP development but is not replacing designers; it makes them more productive.
insights.speaker: Rusafa Shahreen (per Daniel Payne)
insights.so_what: Vendors position AI as a productivity multiplier rather than a headcount substitute.

insights.claim: At the annual GOMACTech Conference in March, government systems engineers heard about data converters, PLLs, transceivers, RF blocks, high-resolution imaging, power converters and rad-hard technologies.
insights.speaker: Daniel Payne
insights.so_what: Lists the IP categories in demand from government system builders.
